### Core rule (CRITICAL) - Model a message (`Message`/`Integration Command`) ONCE, in one `Eventing Package`, in one application. Other applications add a Package Reference and reuse it - never remodel it. - Search the WHOLE solution first for an existing element before creating one. - `Eventing Package` name = C# namespace, so a same-named message modeled separately in another app is a different, unrelated type. - SAVE the designer you just modeled in before switching to another designer to reference it (a Software Factory run also persists pending changes, as a fallback). Unsaved changes are invisible to other designer sessions.
### Workflow 1. Search all applications for an existing `Message`/`Integration Command`/`Domain Event` with this name/intent. 2. If found in another app's `Eventing Package`: save that designer (or run SF) first, then add a Package Reference and reuse it. 3. If not found: create it in the owning application (see ownership rules below) inside an `Eventing Package`. Save (or run SF) before switching designers. 4. Wire publish/subscribe via Intent.Modelers.Services.EventInteractions (`Publish Integration Event`/`Send Integration Command`/`Subscribe Integration Event`/`Subscribe Integration Command`) - see that module's own AI Context for mapping and attach-point rules.
### Anti-patterns - Creating a duplicate because "it isn't visible yet" without checking for an unsaved change or missing Package Reference. - Same event/command modeled differently in two apps. - Modeling a message in a Services Package instead of an `Eventing Package` (unreferenceable).
